description: PR #418 adds a guard (this file, created whole) meant to forbid approximate line anchors like `~12034` anywhere under src/. Rule 1 is right: only comments/string literals are scanned. Rule 2 — the part that decides whether a `~NNN` token is a real anchor or an innocent quantity — is inverted: `_UNIT_TAIL`/`_STOPWORDS` (lines 108-116) is a deny-list of words that do NOT count as a unit, so any `~NNN` followed by anything NOT on that short stopword list is treated as a quantity and silently passed. Two-line repro against src/no_human/core/bounds.py, verified by actually running `pytest tests/test_no_approximate_line_anchors.py` against a real copy of the file: (1) append `# the retry check at ~12034 handles the rebase case` — the suite stays green (27 passed) even though ~12034 is a live forbidden anchor, because 'handles' is not in `_STOPWORDS` so `_UNIT_TAIL` misclassifies it as a unit tail; (2) the control `# see the retry check at ~12034` (nothing trailing) correctly fails 2 tests (`2 failed, 25 passed`), proving the guard's mechanism works when the anchor is bare but not when ordinary prose follows it. The fix is to flip the classifier from a stopword deny-list to a unit ALLOW-list (turns, LOC, %, lines, commits, etc.) so anything not recognizably a unit defaults to 'still an anchor' rather than 'safely a quantity' — which is in fact exactly how a later, still-unmerged follow-up commit on this same PR branch (not part of this case's pinned diff) goes on to fix it. Provenance, precisely stated: PR #418 (`no-human-ai/no_human`) is real and fetchable (`git fetch origin pull/418/head`), but per `gh pr view 418` it was **closed without merging** (`state: CLOSED`, `mergedAt: null`, `mergeCommit: null`) — this case pins the diff to the PR's `bca008c0` revision (merge-base `bbe28a4e`), the state it was in when this guard shipped with the inversion; a later commit on the same (still unmerged) branch fixes the classifier, which is independent corroboration the miss was real, not that it was ever live on `main`. Do not claim 'already-merged into main' anywhere for this case. A prior draft of this description cited four supposedly-still-shipping anchors that turned out to be wrong on inspection (two of the four file paths do not exist in this repo at any revision, and a systematic scan — reimplementing `_find_anchors` and running it over every comment/string literal in all 245 files under src/ at the base commit — found the real false-negative population (19 hits) confined entirely to the 4 files this PR's own diff touches: src/no_human/core/orchestrator.py, src/no_human/vcs/{landability,receipts,recut}.py; re-running the same scan against the PR-head tree found 0 — the PR author hand-fixed every one of those 19 as part of the same diff, so none currently ships uncaught). The corrected, verified framing: the guard's author already had to manually find-and-fix 19 real instances of exactly this false-negative shape while writing this guard, yet the guard's own classifier still cannot catch the next one written the same way — demonstrated here as a mutation (matching the guard's own `test_the_gate_fails_on_a_planted_anchor` methodology), not as a currently-shipping example. Caveat for scoring: this case's diff_override reviewer path is single-turn, no-tools, so it only ever sees this hunk in isolation — it cannot grep src/ for other instances or run the guard's own test suite the way a live review could; the case only measures whether the reviewer can read the classifier logic itself and recognize the inversion.
